what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Not no backend: no tech stack of your own, only the HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
sections.para: An application over sgit vaults rents its backend as commodities: a static host, an encrypted file store, and when needed a model provider or agent platform. The usual primitives remain, in the browser or rented: cached immutable data, a database in WebAssembly, passkeys, append lanes, PKI and models. The constraint makes designs simpler and leaves the server with ciphertext. The gap is giving keys to the client.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: You own the front end, rent the rest, and run the database, identity and encryption in the browser.
sections.para: The constraint is a design tool; the gap is keys to the client; the result is fewer moving parts.

sections.label: Not no backend: no stack of your own
sections.line: A backend still exists, but every part of it is a commodity someone else patches.
sections.para: No application server, framework, database server, password store or queue of your own. sgit makes it possible because it is an encrypted data store a static page can read and write.

sections.label: You keep the primitives
sections.line: Data, database, users, messages, sharing and models all remain without a server of yours.
sections.para: Immutable vault objects cache for ever (RFC 8246). SQLite, DuckDB-Wasm and PGlite run in the browser. Passkeys with the PRF extension give per-user keys with no user table. Append lanes carry messages, sgit's PKI (RSA-OAEP wrapping AES-256-GCM) shares between users, and models run in the browser or behind a host holding the key.

sections.label: Agents: rent the loop
sections.line: For agent loops, rent a cloud agent platform, which also keeps the provenance.
sections.para: Use LLMs so as not to use LLMs: make as much as possible deterministic, and run on the client what can.

sections.label: Fewer moving parts, better design
sections.line: With no server-side data, the constraint pushes simpler designs and a server holding only ciphertext.
sections.para: Data shaped for reading and computed at build time, user state held by the user, and events as lane entries rather than calls to a service that must be up.

sections.label: Vaults as distribution
sections.line: The app itself can live in a vault, served by a static page; moving host is a copy.
sections.para: GitHub Pages suits free tools, demos and docs, but its terms rule out running an online business or commercial SaaS there; use Cloudflare Pages, Netlify or another static host to sell.

sections.label: What is still missing
sections.line: The main gap is a clean way to give keys to the client.
sections.para: Anthropic's SDK disables browser use by default to protect keys. Today's answers: the user's own key, a host that holds it, or a sealed drop to one browser. It looks temporary.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: The figure is illustrative, the backend is rented, and not every application fits.
sections.para: Heavy shared writes, cross-user joins and work with no browser open need more; PRF and on-device model support vary; the server still sees metadata.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The memo of 3 November 2026, standards and library pages, GitHub's limits and sgit 0.21.0's PKI code.
